title: Private Release Gating & Change Management Policy
body:
> **Archived 2025-05-21:** this page is superseded by "Private Release Gating & Change Management Policy" and is kept for reference only.

## Purpose
This policy sets out the **minimum gates** and the **change-management workflow** for shipping Redwood Private releases (VPC and on-prem/air-gapped). It exists to make upgrades **safe by default**, cut down on upgrade-related incidents, and leave behind **auditable artifacts** (plan, prechecks, backup/restore status, approvals, communications).

The requirements here are mandatory. Teams may add stricter checks; any exception needs formal approval (see “Exceptions”).

## Scope
Covers:
- Redwood Private control plane + data plane releases delivered through:
  - `redwood-private-installer` upgrade workflows
  - Helm chart updates (`redwood-helm-charts`)
  - Terraform module updates (`redwood-terraform`) that change version pinning or artifact sources
  - Platform compatibility/policy updates in `redwood`

Does not cover:
- Redwood hosted API releases
- Documentation-only releases

## Definitions
- **Private release**: a versioned bundle of artifacts (installer, charts, images, migrations, compatibility policy) for customer-managed environments.
- **Upgrade plan**: a generated, persisted, auditable plan listing staged steps, required artifacts, dependencies, and rollback entry points.
- **N-1 → N**: the default supported upgrade path for initial GA. (Multi-hop is handled case-by-case.)
- **Blocking precheck**: must pass before proceeding; a failure needs remediation or an approved exception.
- **Warning precheck**: non-blocking, but must be acknowledged in the change record.
- **Change record**: the single source of truth for a planned customer upgrade (internal ticket plus attached artifacts).

## Policy summary (required gates)
A Private release or customer change may go ahead only when:
1) The **supported upgrade path** is enforced by compatibility policy (default: N-1 → N).
2) An **upgrade plan** has been generated and stored (no imperative-only upgrades).
3) All **blocking prechecks** pass.
4) A **backup** has completed successfully (or an approved alternative is documented).
5) **Approvals** are in place (Release Engineering + SRE; Security depending on risk score).
6) **Customer communications** have gone out per risk score and timeline.
7) **Rollback readiness** is confirmed (rollback command, rollback hooks, post-rollback checks).
8) **Auditability** is satisfied (installer logs + audit events retained; support bundle includes upgrade traces).

## Roles and responsibilities
### Required approvers
- **Release Engineering (required)**: checks artifact integrity, CI evidence, and packaging.
  - Default: Connor O’Brien (delegate: Devon Price)
- **SRE (required)**: checks operational safety, monitoring/alerting, and rollback readiness.
  - Default: Sean Gallagher (delegate: Rafael Mendes)

### Conditional reviewers (by risk score)
- **Security/Compliance (conditional)**: needed for regulated environments, backup/restore changes, audit event schema changes, or anything touching secrets/KMS.
  - Default: Naomi Feldman / Marcus Lin
- **Infrastructure (conditional)**: needed for changes to storage backends, networking, or cluster requirements.
  - Default: Irene Choi / Victor Alvarez

## Risk scoring (customer environment)
The rubric below drives communication timelines, approvals, and extra safeguards.

### Risk score = Impact (1–3) + Complexity (1–3) + Environment sensitivity (1–3)
- **Impact**
  - 1: Control-plane-only minor patch; no migrations or Helm ordering changes
  - 2: Rolling restart of data plane or a minor migration; expected <5 min disruption to management operations
  - 3: Schema migrations, control-plane/data-plane sequencing changes, or possible inference impact
- **Complexity**
  - 1: Single component, no dependency changes
  - 2: Multiple components, Helm hook/order changes, or new prechecks
  - 3: New backup mechanism, changed rollback semantics, or artifact source/mirror changes
- **Environment sensitivity**
  - 1: Non-regulated VPC with standard connectivity
  - 2: Regulated VPC (audit/SIEM requirements) or strict customer maintenance windows
  - 3: On-prem/air-gapped, hard customer change-control gates (e.g., CAB), or evidence retention requirements

### Risk tiers
- **Low (3–4)**: Standard gates
- **Medium (5–6)**: Standard + enhanced comms + tabletop rollback drill
- **High (7–9)**: Standard + Security review + pre-upgrade readiness meeting + explicit rollback rehearsal plan

Record both score and tier in the change record.

## Release readiness requirements (pre-cut)
Before a Private release is marked “eligible for customer upgrades”, Release Engineering attaches:
- **CI evidence**: coverage from the private installer integration test matrix (baseline below)
- **Compatibility policy update**: supported upgrade paths listed explicitly
- **Changelog**: customer-facing highlights, known issues, upgrade notes
- **Rollback contract**: unchanged, or documented if changed (changes need SRE + Security review)

### Minimum CI baseline (must pass)
- Kubernetes versions: the current supported set (see test matrix page)
- Scenarios:
  - N-1 → N happy path upgrade
  - Precheck failure injection (at least one blocking check)
  - Migration lock timeout simulation
  - Rollback after a simulated mid-upgrade failure

## Per-customer change workflow (required)
### 1) Open the change record
Open an internal ticket and attach or link:
- Target environment identifiers (customer, region/site, VPC vs on-prem)
- Current → desired versions
- Risk score + tier
- Proposed maintenance window
- On-call coverage plan

### 2) Generate and review the upgrade plan (required)
- Generate:
  - `redwood-private upgrade plan --from <current> --to <target> --output plan.json`
- Review for:
  - Complete artifact list (images/charts/migrations)
  - Stage ordering: control plane finishes before data plane rollouts
  - Rollback entry points and post-rollback verification steps
- Attach `plan.json` and a human-readable summary to the change record.

### 3) Run prechecks (required)
- Run:
  - `redwood-private upgrade precheck --plan plan.json --output precheck-report.json`
- Attach the report to the change record.

#### Blocking prechecks (must pass)
(Full details live in the prechecks spec; this is the policy baseline.)
- **Kubernetes health**: all nodes Ready; no critical system pods in CrashLoopBackOff; API server reachable
- **Control-plane connectivity**: installer reaches control-plane endpoints (or local on-prem endpoints)
- **RBAC/auth**: service accounts and cluster roles present; OIDC/SSO reachable where configured
- **Storage headroom**:
  - Persistent volumes for databases/stateful components have ≥15% free space AND ≥5 GiB free (whichever is larger)
  - Snapshot target has enough space (backend-specific)
- **DB connectivity + privileges**: migration user can take the required locks; bounded lock timeout set
- **Version compatibility**: policy evaluation confirms a supported path (default: N-1 → N)
- **Artifact availability**:
  - Online: registry/chart repo reachable
  - Offline: bundle present with checksum/signature verified
- **TLS/DNS**: no certificates expiring within 7 days; required SANs present; internal endpoints resolve

#### Warning prechecks (must be acknowledged)
- Non-critical capacity warnings (e.g., <30% cluster headroom)
- Optional integrations temporarily unreachable (e.g., SIEM forwarder, non-blocking webhooks)
- Non-default configuration drift (acknowledge + document)

### 4) Backup and restore readiness (required)
- A successful backup is required **before** any irreversible step (e.g., a non-backward-compatible migration).
- Run through the installer:
  - `redwood-private backup run --plan plan.json --output backup-report.json`
- Backup requirements:
  - Encryption on (KMS/HSM where applicable)
  - Restore procedure documented and available to operators
  - Retention: at least 7 days for standard; 30 days for regulated unless the customer requires longer
- Attach `backup-report.json` and backup location metadata to the change record.

### 5) Approval gates (required)
Before “apply” starts:
- **Release Engineering approval** (required): artifacts match the release manifest; CI baseline met; offline/air-gapped bundle verified where relevant.
- **SRE approval** (required): prechecks clean or warnings acknowledged; monitoring/alerts in place for the window; rollback path viable and documented.
- **Security/Compliance approval** (conditional): High risk tier, or changes to audit events, backup handling, encryption defaults, or secret material.

Record each approval in the change record with approver name + timestamp.

### 6) Communications (required)
Requirements depend on risk tier.

#### Internal comms (all tiers)
- Post in `#eng-releases` and `#eng-oncall` at least:
  - T-24h for Medium/High
  - T-2h for Low
- Include customer/site, window, versions, on-call lead, rollback trigger criteria, and the change record link.

#### Customer comms
- **Low**: notify the customer contact at least **48 hours** ahead (or per contract) and confirm the window.
- **Medium**: notify **3 business days** ahead, with expected operator actions and a verification checklist.
- **High**: notify **10 business days** ahead; schedule a readiness call; agree evidence expectations (audit logs, backup proof, rollback plan).

##### Customer email template (copy/paste)
Subject: Redwood Private maintenance window: upgrade to <VERSION>

Hello <Customer Team>,

We plan to upgrade your Redwood Private deployment from <CURRENT_VERSION> to <TARGET_VERSION> during the window below.

- Proposed window: <DATE/TIME> (<TIMEZONE>)
- Expected impact: <e.g., control plane restart; inference data plane unaffected / short rolling restarts>
- Preconditions: preflight checks (cluster health, storage capacity, connectivity) and a backup before any migration.
- Rollback: if upgrade failure conditions are detected, we will roll back to <CURRENT_VERSION> and validate service health.

Success criteria:
- Control plane healthy and responding
- Data plane readiness checks passing
- Upgrade audit events present for compliance logging (if applicable)

Please confirm the window and any change-control requirements we should follow.

Thank you,
<Redwood Contact>

### 7) Execute upgrade (during window)
- Start:
  - `redwood-private upgrade apply --plan plan.json --state-dir <path> --output upgrade-report.json`
- During execution:
  - Follow plan ordering; no skipped steps without SRE approval
  - Health checks after each stage (control plane, then data plane)
  - If a blocking invariant fails, pause and escalate (see “Stop conditions”)

### 8) Stop conditions and escalation
Stop and escalate to SRE + Release Engineering on any of:
- Control plane unavailable >10 minutes with no clear forward progress
- Migration step past its declared plan timeout or showing lock contention beyond thresholds
- Repeated crash loops in upgrade jobs/hooks
- Artifact mismatch (digest differs from manifest)
- Unexpected data plane impact (elevated inference errors)

Escalation: page SRE on-call (Private), notify Release Engineering in `#eng-releases`, and update the customer for Medium/High tier.

### 9) Rollback policy (when invoked)
Rollback is an operational procedure and gets the same rigor as the upgrade.
- Use supported tooling only:
  - `redwood-private upgrade rollback --state-dir <path> --output rollback-report.json`
- Rollback must use stored upgrade state for deterministic reversal, run rollback hooks in order, and pass post-rollback health checks (control plane + data plane).
- Attach the rollback report and final status to the change record.

## Auditability and evidence retention
Keep the following for every customer upgrade event:
- `plan.json` + human summary
- `precheck-report.json`
- `backup-report.json` + backup identifiers
- `upgrade-report.json` and/or state machine logs
- `rollback-report.json` if used
- Sanitized installer logs and referenced artifact manifests
- Audit events: upgrade started, prechecks pass/fail, backup completed, upgrade completed/failed, rollback invoked/completed

Retention: 30 days internal by default; regulated customers per contract, or 90 days if unspecified.

## Post-change requirements
Within 2 business days of completion:
- Update the change record with final status, duration, and deviations
- File and link an incident for any customer-visible impact or rollback
- Capture lessons learned and precheck gaps for backlog triage

## Exceptions
Exceptions must be documented and approved.
- Approvers: Release Engineering lead + SRE lead (both); Security/Compliance as well for regulated/high-tier customers.
- Examples: emergency security patch without time for full comms; customer-mandated window with short lead time; temporary CI gap with compensating controls (e.g., dedicated staging rehearsal).
- Requests must state the gate being bypassed, why it is safe, compensating controls, and the rollback plan and stop conditions.

## Appendix A: Change record checklist (operator-facing)
- [ ] Risk score + tier recorded
- [ ] Upgrade plan generated and attached
- [ ] Blocking prechecks passed; warnings acknowledged
- [ ] Backup completed; restore path documented
- [ ] Approvals captured (RelEng + SRE; Security if required)
- [ ] Customer notified per tier
- [ ] On-call coverage confirmed
- [ ] Upgrade executed with stage verification
- [ ] Rollback readiness confirmed; rollback executed if needed
- [ ] Artifacts retained; support bundle includes upgrade traces

## Appendix B: Internal Slack announcement template
Channel: #eng-releases (cc #eng-oncall)

Private upgrade scheduled
- Customer/site: <NAME> (<VPC/ON-PREM>)
- Window: <START–END> <TZ>
- Version: <CURRENT> → <TARGET>
- Risk tier: <LOW/MED/HIGH> (score: <n>)
- On-call lead: <NAME>
- Plan + prechecks: <LINK>
- Rollback trigger criteria: <BULLETS>

## Ownership
- Policy owner: Release Engineering (Connor O’Brien)
- Operational owner: SRE (Sean Gallagher)
